title: A speech neuroprosthesis reaches 97.5% accuracy after calibration
summary: A man with ALS used a brain-computer interface with machine learning to turn attempted speech into text and synthetic voice. After further training, the system maintained 97.5% accuracy; the study reports more than 248 hours of spontaneous conversation over 32 weeks. Result from one participant with an invasive implant; still experimental.
ai_technology: Neural speech decoding with machine learning

evidence.tested: One participant with ALS in the BrainGate2 trial completed 84 sessions over 32 weeks with over 248 hours of self-paced use; word accuracy was measured per session, with 97.5% maintained after continued data collection.
evidence.unknown: The page does not state the study's limitations, and the result comes from one participant with an invasive implant.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning decoded neural activity into phonemes and then words in real time, with continuous updates, and software generated the voice.
